name: Ladder Up
tagline: From first deposit to first keys, step by step
about: Ladder Up guides first-time buyers from working out what they can really afford, through decoding listings and making offers, to the weeks between an accepted offer and the keys.
persona: You are a straight-talking buyer's advocate who has walked hundreds of first-timers through a purchase: numbers-first, calm about jargon, honest about what is and isn't a big deal.

onboarding.title: Your first home, without the fog
onboarding.subtitle: A few numbers and your market make the maths and the timelines fit you.
bullets: Offer scripts and the path to keys

tools.title: What can I afford?
tools.subtitle: Price ceiling, monthly cost, buffer
tools.prompt: Deposit {deposit}, monthly commitments {outgoings}, buying within {horizon}, income and region from the profile. Produce a kv (comfortable price ceiling, stretch ceiling, deposit % at each, estimated monthly payment at each using a typical current rate range, one-off buying costs to budget), a table (Scenario | Price | Deposit % | Loan | Monthly | Buffer left) with 3 scenarios, bullets on what would raise the ceiling, and a callout on the costs first-timers forget (fees, taxes, moving, furniture).

tools.title: Deposit plan
tools.subtitle: Months to target and how to shorten them
tools.prompt: Target {target}, saved {saved}, saving {monthly} per month. Give a kv (months to target, target date, shortfall if buying within the profile's horizon), a table (Lever | Monthly gain | Effort | Notes) of 6 ways to close the gap faster, steps for setting up the savings structure (accounts, automation, first-buyer schemes to check for the region in general terms), and a callout on not tying the deposit up in anything volatile.

tools.title: Decode a listing
tools.subtitle: Screenshot → agent-speak translated

inputs.label: Screenshot or photo of the listing
Or paste the listing text
inputs.placeholder: Charming period cottage in need of some modernisation…

tools.prompt: Decode this property listing from the screenshot and/or text: {listing}. Asking price: {asking}. Produce a table (Phrase | What it usually means | Question to ask) translating agent-speak, bullets of red flags and green flags spotted, a checklist of 10 things to check at the viewing specific to this property type, and a callout on the single question most likely to change the price.

tools.title: Make an offer
tools.subtitle: Three offer levels and the exact words

inputs.label: What you know
inputs.placeholder: on market 9 weeks, chain-free, two other viewings

tools.prompt: Asking {asking}, context: {context}, buyer position: {position}. Give a table (Offer | % of asking | Rationale | Likely response) with 3 offer levels, steps for the sequence (opening, what to say if rejected, when to walk), a quote with the exact opening message to the agent stating the offer and the buyer's strengths, and a callout on conditions worth attaching (survey, finance, timing).

tools.title: Offer to keys
tools.subtitle: Every stage, who acts, what can slip
tools.prompt: Offer accepted {accepted}, target move {target}, region from the profile. Lay out the stages from acceptance to keys as a table (Week | Stage | Who acts | What you do | Typical delay), a checklist of documents and decisions the buyer must have ready, bullets on the three points where deals most often collapse and how to protect against each, and a callout on when to book removals and give notice.

disclaimer: General information, not financial or mortgage advice; rates, rules and taxes vary by country and lender — confirm figures with a regulated adviser before acting.
